payload:
CORRECTION — do NOT mint a "dev-team Review-Lane QA-Drain PRIMARY-claim actuation defect" row.

Three qa sessions on tick 2026-08-23T21:37Z (TASK_001-WATCHLIST-WRITE-THROUGH-INFRA,
TASK-COWORK-DOC-TRUTH-LAYER-INVENTORY, TASK_003-DOMAIN-MODEL-WATCHLIST-COUNT-FIX) each independently
reported that the dispatch's "promoted review[] -> qa[] this tick" claim was false, and each
recommended minting a FIX row for a dispatcher-side actuation gap (sibling to
FIX-QA-VC-LANEMOVE-PROSE-ONLY-NO-ORCHAPPLY-ACTUATOR). Their VERDICTS were correct and their writes
were correct. Their ROOT-CAUSE INFERENCE is wrong. Acting on it sends a developer to fix a script
that works.

WHAT THEY TESTED: "no commit in orch-state.json history moves these ids into qa[]" — true, and
verified independently 3x. But that test cannot distinguish "never actuated" from "actuated, then
reverted before commit". Both leave identical evidence: no commit, no surviving claimed_at /
claimed_by / drain_source_lane stamps.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED — the promotion DID actuate. docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md
(jump:qa-drain-headdecoupled) has a real actuator, not prose:
    jq ... -f scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq orch-state.json | bash scripts/orch-apply.sh || true
    picked_batch=$(jq -c '[.task_board.qa[] | select(.claimed_at==$t and .claimed_by==$by)]' orch-state.json)
picked_batch is read back FROM THE LIVE FILE after the write. It returned 5 rows; the router built
the 5-way BGFAN-1 fan-out from those row ids. Non-empty picked_batch is only reachable if those rows
were in .task_board.qa[] with a matching claimed_at at that instant. qa[] read 2 -> 7.

THE REVERT: a concurrently-running pm subagent's own unrelated done[] -> done_verified[] write
(commit 54f0cf9b4) carried a FULL-DOCUMENT candidate built from a jq read taken minutes earlier,
before the QA-drain write. It restored the stale qa[]/review[] arrays wholesale. Signature:
`git show 54f0cf9b4 -- docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | grep <row-id>` is EMPTY for all 5 ids — pm
never mentioned them, it just carried a stale copy of the whole array. pm's own work is genuine and
correct; it committed the reverted state, so the QA-drain change never reached any commit.

ROOT CAUSE 1 (real, structural) — scripts/orch-apply.sh CAS window is narrower than the operation
it guards. It captures MTIME_BEFORE at line 116, when orch-apply STARTS — i.e. AFTER the caller's
`jq` already read the file. The caller pipeline is `jq '<transform>' orch-state.json | orch-apply.sh`,
so a candidate built from a stale read applies with no mismatch:
    T0 peer jq reads (qa=2) | T1 our orch-apply writes (qa=7) | T2 peer orch-apply starts,
    MTIME_BEFORE=T1 | T3 peer renames, MTIME_AFTER=T1 -> MATCH -> applies, qa back to 2
Nothing downstream catches it: orch-conservation-check.mjs compares MAGNITUDES (task_total 769=769),
and a lane REVERT preserves every count. Zod passes. Dup-key passes. There is NO lane-placement
invariant anywhere in the write path.
FIX: caller passes the mtime/hash it read at jq time into orch-apply.sh so CAS compares against the
CALLER's snapshot, not orch-apply's own start. Retry-on-exit-2 already exists; it never fires for
this shape.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (real, separate, same line) — the `|| true` on the QA-drain orch-apply pipe silently
swallows a nonzero exit, INCLUDING a genuine CAS exit-2 abort. There is no retry at this call site.
Even once RC-1 is fixed and CAS starts firing correctly, this line would discard the abort and the
subsequent picked_batch read would just come back empty, producing a silent no-op tick.

BLAST RADIUS — smaller than it looks, and the tick still succeeded. 4 of the 5 dispatched qa
sessions ran CONCURRENTLY after the revert, each writing full-document candidates to the same board,
with ZERO mutual clobbering: task_total 769, pending_triage_inbox 12, signal_queue.rows 35 held
byte-stable across all 6 commits of the tick; review[] membership diff shows only intended departures
and nothing re-entering. The hazard is the WIDTH OF THE CALLER'S read->transform gap, not the number
of concurrent writers — pm carried a whole array across minutes of reasoning; the qa agents each
re-derived a single-row move seconds before their pipe. Do not "fix" this by banning concurrent
board writers.

Outcome despite the revert: 3 rows verified through to done_verified[] (428372bd7, 285978c79,
4af44ac60), 1 correctly REFUSED on merits (TASK_001 — AC-5 blocked on a nonexistent TASK_002, AC-7
unverifiable because the deployed mcp-server image 2026-08-23T13:52:50Z predates commit 15:11:08Z),
1 still running at time of filing. All 5 workers re-read state, found the rows in review[], and none
fabricated. A dispatch prompt whose lane premise has gone stale is recoverable when the worker
verifies at source.

ALSO NOTE: those 3 rows went review[] -> done_verified[] DIRECTLY, never entering qa[], so they
consumed no QA_CAP slot. Same cap-bypass shape already recorded for direct review -> qa lane-moves.
Cap-based reasoning about qa throughput undercounts real work in both directions.

ACTION REQUESTED: (a) do not mint the PRIMARY-claim actuation row the 3 qa notebooks/journals
recommend — their journals (qa-S185, qa-S187, sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-27) carry the
wrong attribution and should be annotated; (b) mint instead against scripts/orch-apply.sh for RC-1
(caller-supplied CAS baseline) and against docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md for RC-2 (drop `|| true`,
add retry-on-exit-2 at jump:qa-drain-headdecoupled); (c) both are zone dev-mcp-server / cross-service.
